title: Genetics & Genomics
description: Move from Mendelian segregation to modern genome-scale inference, keeping recombination, gene regulation, and experimental design in view.

outcomes.description: Calculate genotype probabilities under explicit assumptions.
Distinguish association from causal variant evidence.

lesson_objectives.description: Apply segregation rules to pedigrees.
Distinguish genotype frequency from phenotype frequency.
Estimate recombination frequency from progeny counts.
Explain why recombination fraction is a distance proxy with limits.
Interpret cis-regulatory and trans-acting effects.
Choose perturbations that distinguish correlation from mechanism.
Read an association effect with its uncertainty and population context.
Separate statistical association from functional causation.
Compute allele frequencies and Hardy–Weinberg expected genotype counts from observed genotype counts.
Test and interpret a departure from Hardy–Weinberg proportions, including the heterozygote deficit summarized by F.
Estimate carrier frequency for a recessive trait from its incidence and state the assumptions behind the estimate.
Estimate additive genetic, shared-environment and unique-environment variance components from twin correlations under stated assumptions.
Compute a polygenic score from effect sizes and allele dosages and convert variance explained into a correlation.
Evaluate claims about heritability and polygenic prediction, including portability across populations and the difference between population variance and individual destiny.
Determine gene order and interval recombination fractions from three-point testcross progeny counts.
Calculate expected double crossovers, the coefficient of coincidence and interference.
Evaluate why observed recombination underestimates map distance for distant loci and apply a map function to correct it.
Choose a perturbation tool and the controls needed to attribute an effect to the targeted gene.
Quantify knockdown by the ΔΔCt method and state its assumptions.
Plan biological replication and sample size, and distinguish independent replicates from repeated measurements.
State the three core instrumental-variable assumptions and explain why genetic variants can satisfy them.
Compute a Wald-ratio causal estimate with its approximate standard error and convert a log-odds estimate to an odds ratio.
Evaluate an MR result for weak instruments and pleiotropy, and distinguish it from an observational association.
Predict phenotype ratios for two independently assorting genes, including the modified ratios produced by epistasis (9:3:4, 9:7, 12:3:1 and 15:1).
Test an observed ratio against competing genetic hypotheses with a chi-square goodness-of-fit test.
Use complementation tests and epistasis analysis to decide whether mutations affect the same gene and to order genes in a pathway.
Recognize X-linked recessive and dominant inheritance in pedigrees and compute transmission probabilities to sons and daughters.
Update a carrier probability with Bayes' rule using the evidence of unaffected sons.
Evaluate how incomplete penetrance, new mutations and X-inactivation complicate pedigree inference.
Trace the gametes produced by nondisjunction in meiosis I versus meiosis II and the resulting zygotes (normal, trisomic or monosomic).
Calculate expected aneuploid gamete frequencies from per-meiosis error rates, and compare age groups with a relative risk and a risk difference.
Evaluate evidence about why segregation errors increase with maternal age, distinguishing a description from a mechanism.
Estimate a mutation rate from the fraction of parallel cultures that contain no mutants, using the Poisson zero class.
Explain how the fluctuation test distinguishes mutations that arise before selection from mutations induced by it, using the variance of mutant counts across cultures.
Calculate somatic mutation accumulation from a per-year rate and evaluate what mutation counts in aging stem cells do and do not show.
Normalize read counts for library size (counts per million) and compute a log₂ fold change.
Explain why testing many genes at once requires false-discovery control, and apply the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure to a short list of p-values.
Design an expression comparison with biological replicates, balanced batches and a pre-specified analysis, and evaluate what a fold change does not show.
Summarize genotype data by ancestry and case status with counts and mean allele dosage, and convert dosage to allele frequency.
Compute an allelic odds ratio and chi-square statistic from allele counts and compare the result with a multiple-testing threshold.
Evaluate confounding by ancestry with a stratified analysis, and decide which association signals warrant follow-up.
Narrow an association signal to a credible set of candidate variants from approximate Bayes factors, assuming a single causal variant.
Quantify allele-specific expression in heterozygous samples and state what an imbalance does and does not show.
Design a staged follow-up, from cell type to variant-to-gene link to perturbation with rescue, naming the confounders and the claim each stage can support.

duration.equivalent_structure: Proposed 14-week undergraduate scope only. The four compact prototype units sit in weeks 1, 4, 9 and 11 beside original lessons on inheritance, mapping, population genetics, mutation, gene regulation, expression measurement, association and causal inference; week 12 is a synthetic-data association lab and week 14 a follow-up design lesson with the course case. All activities are open, ungraded practice. There are no graded homework sets, exams or project, and workload has not been measured, so this schedule is not evidence of semester equivalence.

weeks.title: Gene interaction: epistasis, complementation and modified ratios
Sex linkage, pedigrees and Bayesian carrier risk
Three-point mapping, interference and map functions
Chromosome segregation errors: nondisjunction, aneuploidy and maternal age
Mutation rates, the fluctuation test and somatic mutation
Gene regulation and designing a controlled perturbation experiment
Measuring gene expression: normalization and false discoveries
Virtual lab: an association study with population structure
Mendelian randomization and causal inference from genetic variants
From association to mechanism: designing the follow-up of a locus

workload.basis: Not measured. Legacy nominal credit and display-time labels are not retained as workload estimates.

lessons.title: Segregation, penetrance, and probability
lessons.worked_example: For two heterozygous parents Aa × Aa, the child genotype probabilities are 1/4 AA, 1/2 Aa, and 1/4 aa. A recessive phenotype with full penetrance has probability 1/4 only if both parents are carriers.

lessons.title: Linkage and recombination mapping
lessons.worked_example: If 180 of 1,000 offspring are recombinant in a testcross, r = 0.18 and the loci are approximately 18 cM apart for a short interval.

lessons.title: Gene regulation and causal perturbation
lessons.worked_example: If editing a promoter lowers RNA and protein, a promoter-independent cDNA rescue that restores phenotype supports a causal link between reduced gene product and phenotype, while not excluding every downstream effect.

lessons.title: Genomics, association, and variant interpretation
lessons.worked_example: A replicated association with a noncoding SNP narrows a region, not necessarily a gene. Fine-mapping and cell-type-specific perturbation can distinguish plausible regulatory mechanisms.

lessons.title: Allele frequencies, Hardy–Weinberg expectations and what a departure can mean
lessons.worked_example: Count allele copies and compare observed genotypes with random-union expectations. p = (2 × 420 + 360) / 2000 = 0.60; expected 360/480/160; χ² = 62.5 with 1 df; F = 0.25; incidence 1/2500 gives carriers 2pq = 0.0392.

lessons.title: Heritability, polygenic scores and the limits of genetic prediction
lessons.worked_example: Under the equal-environments and additivity assumptions, the synthetic twin correlations give h² = 2 × (0.5 − 0.3) = 0.40, c² = 0.10, e² = 0.50; PGS = 0.23 from four synthetic variants; R² = 0.08 corresponds to r = 0.28.

lessons.title: Three-point mapping: gene order, map distance, interference and why distances do not simply add
lessons.worked_example: In the synthetic cross the rarest classes identify b as the middle gene; r(a–b) = 0.114, r(b–c) = 0.112; expected double crossovers 12.8, observed 8, so interference is 0.37; the observed a–c fraction 0.21 undercounts the summed 0.226.

lessons.title: Designing a controlled gene-perturbation experiment: tools, controls, quantification and replication
lessons.worked_example: Synthetic qPCR gives ΔCt 6.0 (control) and 8.3 (knockdown), ΔΔCt = 2.3 and relative expression 0.203 (80% knockdown); with σ = 0.5 and δ = 1.0, the normal approximation gives about 4 independent biological replicates per group, and an exact t-test calculation 6.

lessons.title: Mendelian randomization: using genetic variants to test whether an exposure causes an outcome
lessons.worked_example: A variant raising the exposure by 0.1 and the outcome log-odds by 0.05 per allele gives a Wald ratio of 0.50 (odds ratio 1.65 per unit, SE about 0.10); its F-statistic is 100, while a variant with effect 0.02 and SE 0.01 has F = 4, a weak instrument.

lessons.title: Gene interaction: epistasis, complementation and modified dihybrid ratios
lessons.worked_example: An F2 of 96 purple and 64 white rejects 3:1 (χ² = 19.2) but fits 9:7 (χ² = 0.91); a mouse F2 of 105:39:48 fits 9:3:4 (χ² = 0.33, 2 df); complementation places two white mutations in different genes, and daf-16 is required for daf-2 longevity in worms.

modules.title: Sex linkage and Bayesian carrier risk

lessons.title: Sex-linked inheritance, pedigrees and Bayesian carrier risk
lessons.worked_example: With a prior carrier probability of 1/2, three unaffected sons give a posterior of 1/9 and a next-son risk of 1/18; two unaffected sons give 1/5; at 80% penetrance a carrier's son is unaffected with probability 0.6, so each unaffected son is weaker evidence.

lessons.title: Chromosome segregation errors: nondisjunction, aneuploidy and maternal age
lessons.worked_example: With nondisjunction in 4% of meioses, 2% of products are disomic for meiosis I errors and 1% for meiosis II errors; a synthetic registry gives trisomy risks of 1.5 and 12 per 1000 (relative risk 8, risk difference 10.5 per 1000); 38 of 50 centromeric-marker results point to maternal meiosis I.

lessons.title: Mutation rates, the fluctuation test and somatic mutation with age
lessons.worked_example: 22 of 50 cultures without mutants give m = 0.821 and a rate of 4.10 per 10⁹ divisions; independent cultures (0, 1, 0, 2, 0, 0, 13 and 0) have a variance-to-mean ratio of 10.1, aliquots 0.86; 40 mutations per year give 3000 by age 75, about 45 in coding sequence.

lessons.title: Measuring gene expression: read counts, normalization, fold change and false discoveries
lessons.worked_example: 450 of 25,000,000 reads is 18 CPM against 20 in control, a log₂ fold change of -0.152 although raw reads rose 1.5-fold; 20,000 null tests at p < 0.05 give about 1,000 false positives; Benjamini–Hochberg at q = 0.05 calls 5 of ten example genes and Bonferroni 1.

modules.title: Virtual laboratory: association study with population structure

lessons.title: Virtual lab 1: a case–control association study with population structure
lessons.worked_example: Pooled SYN1 alleles give an odds ratio of 2.79 and χ² = 12.0, passing the Bonferroni threshold of 0.0167, yet within each population the odds ratio is 1.00, so the signal is confounded by ancestry; SYN2 has an odds ratio of 2.33 pooled, stratified and Mantel–Haenszel, χ² = 8.3, and is a candidate that needs replication; SYN3 shows no association.

lessons.title: From an association signal to a mechanism: designing the follow-up of a locus
lessons.worked_example: Bayes factors 600, 300, 60, 30, 10 give PIPs 0.60, 0.30, 0.06, 0.03, 0.01 and a 95% credible set of 3 variants; 140 of 200 reference reads give z = 5.66 for allele-specific expression, which localizes an effect to a haplotype, and a base edit in isogenic cells with independent clones and rescue is needed to test the variant.

grading_policy.attempt_policy: Unlimited formative retries; no summative grade is awarded.
grading_policy.solution_release: Public practice solutions may be shown after an attempt. They are not production exam keys.
grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.
grading_policy.appeals: No instructor review workflow is implemented; report ambiguous practice items to repository maintainers.

accessibility.diagram_policy: The seed package contains no imported diagrams; newly authored diagrams require descriptions and individual license tracking.
known_issues: Unicode equations require structured mathematical alternatives and assistive-technology review.

history.summary: Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.

Added two original lessons (Hardy–Weinberg proportions and departures, carrier frequency, twin-based heritability and polygenic scores) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Added two original lessons (three-point mapping with interference and map functions, and designing a controlled gene-perturbation experiment with ΔΔCt quantification and sample size) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Added an original lesson on Mendelian randomization (instrument assumptions, Wald ratio, instrument strength and pleiotropy) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Assessments with items now also list the course outcomes those items assess, derived from each item's lesson objective and that objective's outcome links. The rubric-only case lists none, and neither do the 4 prototype-unit assessments, whose objectives are not yet linked to an outcome. No readings, items or keys changed. The syllabus was regenerated from the manifest: it states the current version, lists every lesson with its item and card counts, and describes the current practice and limitations (it still described only the four original units). The course limitations shown to learners were also updated: they still described one formative check per lesson and the original numerical rules. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Fixes from an AI-assisted check of 0.4.1 (docs/reviews/ai-assisted/genetics-0.4.1.md), which recomputed every practice answer from its stated data and read each lesson: the perturbation lesson recommended 4 replicates per group right after noting that the normal approximation runs low (an exact t-test calculation gives about 66% power at 4 and needs 6), and its worked example, item solution and card now say so; the mapping lesson now gives Kosambi's 22.4 cM instead of 'intermediate values'; one item and one worked example use the unrounded 0.226; one heritability sentence was reworded. This was not a human review; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added a proposed 14-week schedule; six original lessons (gene interaction and epistasis; sex linkage and Bayesian carrier risk; nondisjunction and aneuploidy with maternal age; mutation rates, the fluctuation test and somatic mutation; measuring gene expression with normalization and false-discovery control; and the follow-up design of an association locus with fine-mapping and allele-specific expression); a synthetic-data case–control association lab (population structure, stratified analysis and a multiple-testing threshold); and common-mistakes sections for lessons 5 to 8. Four link-only references were added (records checked; three abstracts read, one scanned paper not read). All activities remain ungraded practice; the package remains partial and unreviewed, gives no counselling or medical advice, and makes no claim about any person.

limitations: Four compact legacy units are preserved beside twelve original readings, including one synthetic-data virtual lab; this package is not equivalent to a full university semester.

A proposed 14-week schedule exists but is unmeasured and unreviewed. There is one synthetic-data virtual lab and no substantive homework sequence, laboratory sequence, midterm, cumulative final, or graded integrative project.

Practice items are short formative checks (two per prototype unit and six to seven per original lesson); they do not demonstrate comprehensive outcome coverage or mastery, and objective associations remain provisional.
Bloom labels and structured prerequisite edges are initial authoring classifications awaiting subject-matter review.
Question answers and solution feedback are intentionally public practice authoring specifications, not restricted exam keys.

Of the 49 numerical answers in this package, one requires a unit, two check significant figures and none checks dimensions; the others accept a number within a stated tolerance, with the unit optional.
Total workload and weekly duration are unknown; former nominal credit values and hardcoded reading times do not establish workload.
Risk calculations for families are synthetic teaching examples; this package gives no genetic-counselling or medical advice and says nothing about any person's risk.
intentionally_omitted: Graded assessments and a laboratory sequence are not authored yet (one synthetic-data virtual lab exists); the original lessons extend a partial package.
